label: GO after a rare-rewarded a2 trial (a2->S1, rewarded), late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO steps, never at D1 or D2. The previous trial was rewarded (98.8% of activation mass), was rare (83%), and its choice was a2 (89%); that is, the agent chose a2, landed in S1 and got rewarded. The feature is also strongly gated by episode time: no activity before about trial 45, and the rate climbs steeply over trials 70-99. Value is low and the policy leans strongly toward a2 when it fires (choice logit < -4; model_act a2 carries 94.5% of mass). This predicate uses only observed history (ep_trial is not an input, so the agent would have to track elapsed time). It captures 80% of the activation mass at dev precision 0.79, but recall by count is only 0.50: the misses are mostly weak activations (bottom quartile) at other late GO steps after rewarded a2 trials, including common ones. Adding the upcoming choice action==2 raises precision to 0.92 but lowers mass recall, so it was left out. Magnitude is largest when the rare-rewarded a2 trial is immediately preceded and followed by sticking with a2 near the episode end. It does not fire after unrewarded trials, after a1 choices, or outside GO.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a2 S1 r, a2 S1 u, a2 S2 r) and trial before (GO: a2 S1 u, a2 S1 r, a2 S2 r); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
